title: Si: vicinal-wafer atomic step bunches as maskless wordline template
idea: Cut Si(111) wafers at a precise miscut so a UHV/H2 anneal bunches atomic steps into a self-ordered array whose pitch is set by the miscut angle (e.g. 24 nm); selectively nucleate an oxide or metal along the step edges to form the dense wordline hardmask with no exposure at all for that array layer.
why: Litho/capital (fact 4): the crystal lattice becomes the ruler, deleting one EUV or SAQP line layer (~4-8 steps) in the array; ~3-5% wafer-cost cut if edge-roughness is controllable.

title: Al: self-ordered anodic alumina pores replace EUV capacitor-hole patterning
idea: Deposit Al over the storage-node landing pads, pre-texture with a coarse DUV guide pattern, then anodize so pores self-organize at a voltage-set pitch (~2.5 nm/V) and grow straight to AR >100:1 with no plasma etch; line the pores with TiN/ZrO2/TiN to form the capacitors.
why: Facts 1 and 4: removes the EUV hole layer and the slowest high-AR dry etch while reaching AR beyond 115 for more Cs; ~30-40% capacitor-module cost cut claimed.

title: Ti: oxidize the TiN electrode into its own rutile dielectric
idea: Instead of ALD-depositing ZrO2 and then a top electrode, convert the outer 4-6 nm of the TiN bottom electrode into rutile TiO2 (k~80-100) with an ozone/radical oxidation that co-incorporates Al from a pre-dosed monolayer to suppress leakage; one conversion step replaces hundreds of ALD cycles and is conformal at any AR.
why: Fact 1 (k~70 needed) plus throughput: deletes the longest ALD tool-time step of the capacitor module; conversion is self-conformal so deeper holes cost no extra time. Leakage of TiO2 is the open risk.

title: Fe: magnetically chained magnetite nanoparticles as wordline etch masks
idea: Spin a monodisperse Fe3O4 nanoparticle ink into coarse DUV guide trenches, apply an in-plane magnetic field so particles chain into parallel lines with spacing set by dipole repulsion, then sinter into an iron-oxide etch mask that strips in dilute acid.
why: Litho capital: field-directed assembly substitutes for SADP/SAQP on periodic array lines; each avoided multipatterning loop saves ~4-8 steps and an EUV pass. Defectivity is the risk.

title: Zn: self-evaporating ZnO scaffold opens 3D-DRAM tier gaps
idea: Stack Si/ZnO tiers, cut the vertical slits, then anneal in hydrogen so ZnO is reduced and the high-vapor-pressure Zn evaporates out through the slits, leaving clean cavities for gate and capacitor fill with no selective wet or radical etch.
why: Fact 2: selective lateral SiGe removal across 26+ tiers is a yield/throughput blocker; a thermal sacrificial removal is fully parallel, batchable and has effectively infinite selectivity. Zn contamination control is the risk.

title: Sn: liquid-tin skin printing of 2D SnO p-channel periphery
idea: Touch a wafer to a liquid Sn-Ga alloy under controlled O2 so its self-limiting, atomically thin SnO surface skin transfers in one stroke over 300 mm; pattern it into p-type TFTs stacked above the array to host part of the decoder and sense-amp periphery.
why: Fact 7 (periphery ~49% of die): stacking periphery in BEOL layers made by a vacuum-free heated-bath tool (vs a ~$5M CVD) could reclaim 20-30% die area; complements n-type oxides from prior work.

title: C: diamond-armored nanoimprint templates for repetitive array layers
idea: Coat nanoimprint replica templates with a thin conformal CVD-diamond skin so they survive >10x more imprints and resist particle damage, then use step-and-repeat nanoimprint for the 3-4 most periodic array layers (holes, lines) instead of EUV.
why: Fact 4: NIL tools cost ~1/5-1/10 of EUV in capital and energy; template wear and defects are NIL's blocker for DRAM, which diamond's hardness and inertness attack.

title: N: nitrogen-terminated surfaces steer ALD into self-aligned contacts
idea: Expose the wafer to an NH3 plasma chemistry that N-terminates the dielectric but not the Si/metal landing pads, then use precursors that cannot nucleate on N-terminated SiN so liner and contact metal grow only on the pads (area-selective deposition), deleting the contact litho and etch.
why: Fact 4: removes 1-2 mask layers per contact level and their overlay budget; ~3-5% wafer-cost cut and better contact yield at tight pitch.

title: O: oxidation volume expansion halves pitch instead of SAQP
idea: Print poly-Si lines at relaxed pitch, then thermally oxidize: SiO2 occupies ~2.2x the volume of the Si consumed, so the growing sidewall oxide narrows each gap by a kinetically controlled amount, producing sub-litho trenches that are filled with the second line set.
why: Replaces spacer deposition/etch loops of SAQP with a 100+-wafer batch furnace step; ~30-50% fewer patterning steps on those layers at a fraction of the tool capital.

title: Na: epitaxial NaCl release layers for single-crystal tier transfer
idea: Grow epitaxial NaCl on a reusable crystalline donor, grow single-crystal oxide channel or ferroelectric films on the salt, bond them to the CMOS wafer and dissolve the salt with a small water mist to release the film; the donor is reused hundreds of times.
why: Facts 2 and 4: high-quality stacked tiers without high-temperature processing on the CMOS wafer and without buying a new single-crystal substrate per tier; donor cost amortized ~100x.

title: Mg: magnesiothermic reduction turns stubby oxide posts into porous capacitors
idea: Pattern short SiO2 posts (AR ~15), expose them to Mg vapor at ~650 C so SiO2 + 2Mg -> Si + 2MgO forms a nanoporous Si sponge, strip the MgO, then coat with ALD dielectric and electrode; surface area rises ~10x without a high-aspect-ratio etch.
why: Fact 1: decouples capacitance from aspect ratio, so the 60-75:1 etch (the costliest capacitor step) shrinks to ~15:1 or Cs rises several-fold at the same height.

title: Ca: lattice-matched CaF2/Si epitaxial superlattice for strain-free 3D tiers
idea: Grow alternating single-crystal Si and CaF2 layers (~0.6% mismatch) in one pump-down; CaF2 serves as tier isolation and as a sacrificial layer that etches with high selectivity to Si, avoiding the strain accumulation that caps SiGe/Si stacks.
why: Fact 2: strain-free stacking allows 50+ tiers in a single deposition run without relaxation defects, past the ~26-tier break-even.

title: S: in-tunnel sulfurization converts Mo into lateral MoS2 access channels
idea: Inside the lateral tunnels of a 3D-DRAM stack, ALD a few-angstrom Mo or MoO3 film around a pre-formed gate, then flow H2S or sulfur vapor so it converts in place to MoS2, giving an atomically thin lateral access transistor exactly where 2D-material transfer is impossible.
why: Facts 2 and 3: gas-phase conversion reaches deep lateral cavities, and MoS2's wide gap shrinks the leakage tail to extend refresh intervals.

title: H: hydrogen-blister peeling stacks tiers from one reusable donor
idea: Implant H into a donor Si wafer, bond to the target, split at the blister plane to transfer a 30-50 nm single-crystal tier, smooth by H2 anneal, then repeat 26+ times from the same donor with low-temperature device steps between transfers.
why: Fact 2: replaces long SiGe/Si epitaxial stacks with repeated layer transfer; tier quality equals bulk Si and one donor feeds many tiers.

title: Ni: nickel-seeded lateral crystallization of cheap amorphous tier stacks
idea: Deposit fast PECVD amorphous-Si/oxide stacks, open one vertical seed slit, add Ni there so NiSi2 fronts sweep laterally through every a-Si layer at ~550 C converting it to needle-like single-grain Si; the Ni-rich front ends in a sacrificial region that is cut away.
why: Fact 2: amorphous deposition is ~10x faster and cheaper than epitaxy and tolerates 100+ tiers; MILC gives near-crystalline mobility. Residual Ni leakage is the risk.

title: Cu: hybrid-bond DRAM arrays to periphery from depreciated US fabs
idea: Make only the cell array in the leading-edge DRAM fab and fabricate the periphery (~49% of die) on 28-40 nm logic wafers in existing, depreciated U.S. foundries, joining the two with Cu-Cu hybrid wafer bonding.
why: Facts 4 and 7: roughly doubles array bits per expensive DRAM wafer and uses idle U.S. capacity with near-zero new capex for the periphery half.

title: Bi: capillary-infiltrated molten Bi-Sn fills high-AR cavities
idea: Coat the array with a thin wetting liner, flood with molten Bi-Sn eutectic (~140 C) under gas pressure so it wicks into capacitor top-plate cavities and plugs, then wipe the excess with a heated blade before it freezes; Bi's solidification expansion offsets shrink voids.
why: Replaces slow CVD SiGe/W top-plate and plug fill with an atmospheric tool ~1/10 the cost, and removes tungsten (China ~80%) from those layers.

title: Te: thermal-threshold chalcogenide resist writes sub-diffraction imprint masters
idea: Use phase-transition mastering: a Ge-Sb-Te or incomplete-oxide resist changes phase only above a sharp temperature threshold, so a cheap 405 nm laser writer prints features ~1/4 of its spot size; selective development yields DRAM array masters for nanoimprint.
why: Master writing today needs multi-million-dollar e-beam tools and days per plate; thermal-threshold writing (Blu-ray mastering heritage) cuts master cost and time ~10x.

title: He: helium-free fab using hydrogen backside cooling and recapture
idea: Replace He as electrostatic-chuck backside gas with H2 (similar thermal conductivity) or Ne, switch leak checks to H2/N2 forming-gas sniffers, and recover residual He from tool exhaust with membranes, decoupling uptime from Qatari supply.
why: Resource chokepoint: Qatar's ~30% helium is offline and etch/deposition tools idle without it; this keeps capital tools productive.

title: K: ion-exchanged glass panels replace silicon HBM interposers
idea: Build HBM interposers on 510x515 mm thin glass panels toughened by K+/Na+ ion exchange, laser-drill through-glass vias, and pattern redistribution layers with panel-class tools instead of a 300 mm silicon interposer line.
why: Fact 6 (HBM TSV tax): a panel carries ~4x the area of a 300 mm wafer on cheaper tools; low-loss glass also lowers I/O energy.

title: La: LaB6 multi-cathode e-beam writes periphery without mask sets
idea: Use arrays of thousands of LaB6 cathodes in a multi-beam direct-write tool for the irregular periphery and low-volume layers, eliminating mask sets and enabling rapid design spins in a small U.S. fab.
why: Mask sets cost $10-20M per node; direct write removes them and EUV from non-repetitive layers, making a low-volume startup memory line economic.

title: Cr: chrome-free interference lithography prints periodic cell arrays
idea: Because cell arrays are perfectly periodic, expose them with multi-beam 193 nm immersion interference (no photomask, no chrome absorber) to produce line and hole lattices, using one cheap trim mask for array edges.
why: Interference tools cost ~1/10 of a scanner and need no mask; with one spacer doubling they reach ~20 nm half-pitch for the array.

title: Hf: one HfZrO deposition serves gate, capacitor and liner
idea: In a vertical-channel 4F2 cell, deposit a single conformal HfZrO film that wraps the channel (gate dielectric), continues over the storage node (capacitor dielectric) and seals the stack (liner), then tune each region's phase with localized anneal.
why: Process consolidation: three dielectric modules collapse into one ALD step plus anneal, cutting tool types and cycle time ~10%.

title: F: anhydrous HF vapor dip-out frees capacitor pillars without rinse
idea: Remove the oxide capacitor mold with anhydrous HF plus alcohol vapor at reduced pressure instead of a wet buffered-HF dip, DI rinse and spin-dry; no liquid touches the pillars, so there is no capillary collapse either.
why: Water: the mold dip-out and its rinse go from liters per wafer to ~0 (>10x for the capacitor module); with no stiction, AR can climb past 100:1 for more Cs (fact 1).

title: Ar: gas-cluster ion beam planarization replaces slurry CMP
idea: Planarize dielectric and metal overburden with argon gas-cluster ion beams whose lateral sputtering smooths high spots, using in-line height maps to dose locally; no slurry, pads or post-CMP scrub.
why: Water: CMP plus post-CMP clean uses ~10-20% of fab UPW; GCIB cuts that module ~100% and removes slurry consumables. Throughput is the risk.

title: C: closed-loop supercritical CO2 removes post-etch residues
idea: Replace aqueous/semi-aqueous post-etch residue removal and its DI rinse with supercritical CO2 carrying a few percent chelating co-solvent in a pressure cell; the CO2 is recompressed and recycled >95%.
why: Water: post-etch cleans recur dozens of times per DRAM flow, and their water drops >10x; zero surface tension also protects high-AR pillars and 3D tiers.

title: O: downstream atomic-oxygen ash ends sulfuric-peroxide resist strips
idea: Strip implant and patterning resists with a remote O-radical plasma preceded by an H2/N2 radical crust-break step, eliminating hot sulfuric-peroxide (SPM) baths and their rinses.
why: Water and chemicals: SPM strips and hot rinses are heavy UPW and acid users; dry strip cuts that module's water >10x and removes sulfuric waste treatment.

title: H: remote atomic-hydrogen pre-clean replaces RCA wet benches
idea: Remove native oxide, carbon and metal-organic residue before epi and gate steps with remote atomic hydrogen at 300-500 C plus NF3/NH3 radical oxide removal in the same vacuum cluster, so wafers go from etch to deposition without a wet bench.
why: Water: RCA-type cleans are the largest category of UPW use; a dry pre-clean cuts it >10x and frees bench floor space.

title: N: cryogenic nitrogen aerosol lifts particles with zero liquid
idea: Sweep an expanding jet of N2/Ar cryogenic aerosol (frozen micro-particles) across the wafer so momentum transfer lifts nanoparticles, after which the aerosol sublimes with no residue; use it wherever megasonic DI scrubs are used today.
why: Water: particle-removal scrubs drop to zero water, and the gentle dry action avoids toppling fragile capacitor pillars.

title: Cl: ClF3 vapor carves 3D-DRAM lateral recesses dry
idea: Use low-temperature ClF3 gas-phase etching, which removes SiGe with very high selectivity to Si, oxide and nitride, to cut lateral recesses across 26-100 tiers in one batch vacuum step instead of wet selective etch and long rinses.
why: Fact 2 plus water: deep-slit wet etches need long rinses and suffer stiction; dry recess cuts that module's water ~100% and enables taller stacks.

title: Xe: 172 nm excimer photons clean wafers inside load-locks
idea: Mount Xe2* excimer VUV lamps inside tool load-locks so every wafer gets a ~30 s photolysis in N2 that breaks organic and airborne molecular contamination before each deposition, replacing routine wet pre-cleans between steps.
why: Water: removes dozens of inter-step wet cleans with zero added queue time; those steps' water falls ~100%.

title: Ti: getter-pumped vacuum wafer highway so wafers never see air
idea: Link etch, deposition and anneal tools with a titanium-getter/NEG-pumped vacuum transport spine and sealed vacuum carriers, so native oxide and airborne contamination never form and most cleans disappear; cleanroom air shrinks to tool-scale vacuum.
why: Water: attacks the two biggest users at once, cleans and cleanroom HVAC (humidification and chilled water), toward a 10x fab-level cut; also shrinks cleanroom capex.

title: Si: plasma dicing and dry thinning for HBM die
idea: Finish thinning HBM DRAM wafers with high-rate SF6 plasma instead of wet polishing, and singulate with deep reactive-ion plasma dicing instead of water-cooled blade sawing; die edges come out chip-free.
why: Fact 6 (HBM yield -20-30%): chipping and microcracks fall; grinding/sawing water and slurry for the module fall >10x.

title: Sn: tin-oxo resist doubles as hardmask, leaves as stannane
idea: Vapor-deposit a Sn-oxo-carbon resist, dry-develop it, keep the remaining SnOx as the etch hardmask, then remove it with an H2 plasma that converts tin into volatile SnH4 (the trick used to clean EUV collectors).
why: Water: no spin solvent, TMAH develop, rinse or wet strip on each patterned layer (>10x litho-module water cut) and one fewer hardmask deposition per layer.

title: Zn: vapor-grown zinc MOF films as dry-developed resist
idea: Convert an ALD ZnO film into a ZIF-8 metal-organic framework by exposure to 2-methylimidazole vapor; e-beam/EUV exposure alters the framework so a reactive gas removes exposed or unexposed areas, giving a solvent-free, water-free, metal-rich resist.
why: Water: removes the wet track (spin, develop, rinse) from each litho layer, >10x water and solvent reduction for that module, with higher etch resistance than organic resists.

title: Al: aluminum-infiltrated block copolymers pattern capacitor holes dry
idea: Thermally anneal a block copolymer into a hexagonal hole lattice matched to cell pitch, infiltrate one block with trimethylaluminum/ozone vapor pulses to make AlOx, then O2-plasma away the polymer to leave a dry hardmask.
why: Water and litho: replaces the EUV hole layer and its wet track with self-assembly plus vapor infiltration that uses negligible water (>10x cut for that layer).

title: S: sublimable sulfur scaffolds support tall structures, then vanish
idea: Fill cavities and slits with molten elemental sulfur (melts ~115 C) as a temporary mechanical support and planarizer during subsequent steps, then sublime it away in vacuum at ~150-200 C, leaving clean cavities.
why: Water: replaces sacrificial-oxide fill plus wet strip and rinse in 3D-DRAM and capacitor flows (~100% water cut for the module), and props very tall stacks against collapse.

title: Ge: sacrificial germanium self-erases as GeO vapor
idea: Use pure Ge sacrificial layers in tier stacks; after the slit opens, lightly oxidize the exposed Ge and anneal at ~500-600 C so Ge + GeO2 -> 2GeO(g) volatilizes, propagating laterally and erasing the layer selective to Si and SiO2 with no etchant gas or liquid.
why: Fact 2 plus water: lateral sacrificial removal with no wet etch, rinse or stiction (~100% module water cut) in a batch furnace.

title: Ca: dry lime beds turn fab fluorine into resaleable fluorspar
idea: Replace water-fed local wet scrubbers on etch/CVD exhaust with a plasma abatement front end plus heated CaO/Ca(OH)2 granular beds that capture HF and fluorine as CaF2, sold back to HF producers as synthetic fluorspar.
why: Water: wet scrubbers are ~5-10% of fab water and drop to ~0; it also closes the loop on fluorspar, a critical mineral.

title: Fe: La-Fe-Si magnetocaloric heat pumps enable dry-air heat rejection
idea: Use La(Fe,Si)13 magnetocaloric solid-state heat pumps to lift tool-coolant waste heat from ~20 C to ~50 C so it can be dumped through dry air coolers year-round, eliminating evaporative cooling towers.
why: Water: cooling-tower evaporation is often the largest consumptive water use in a fab (~25-40%) and drops to ~0. Heat-pump efficiency at scale is the risk.

title: Na: salt-hydrate thermal batteries shift heat rejection to night
idea: Store daytime chiller heat in sodium-sulfate-based salt-hydrate tanks tuned to melt near 30 C, then discharge overnight through dry coolers when ambient is lower, so the fab needs no evaporative cooling even in Arizona or Texas.
why: Water: makes dry cooling viable in U.S. Sun Belt fab clusters, cutting cooling water to ~0 without a heat-pump energy penalty.

title: B: boron-doped diamond anodes close the rinse-water loop
idea: Pass spent rinse water through boron-doped diamond anodes that electrochemically mineralize organics and oxidizable species with no chemical dosing, then electrodeionize and return it to UPW grade at point of use instead of discharging it.
why: Water: raises recycle from ~40-60% to ~95%, cutting net withdrawal ~10x for the remaining wet steps.

title: P: vapor phosphonate monolayer doping replaces implant-and-strip loops
idea: Form a phosphorus-bearing self-assembled monolayer from the vapor phase on Si exposed through a reusable hardmask (not resist), cap it and spike-anneal to drive a shallow conformal dopant profile, even inside 3D tunnels that implant beams cannot reach.
why: Water: each implant layer (10+ in DRAM) normally needs resist coat, strip and clean; vapor doping removes that water (>10x for the doping module) and enables doping of lateral 3D cells.

title: Mo: subtractive dry-etched molybdenum metal layers with no CMP
idea: Deposit blanket Mo, pattern it with dry Cl2/O2 etch, then gap-fill with flowable dielectric cured by UV, the reverse of Cu/W damascene, so the metal layer needs no CMP and no post-CMP clean.
why: Water: deletes CMP and post-CMP scrub on each metal layer (>10x for the module); resources: removes tungsten (China ~80%).

title: Se: xerographic charge-image patterning with dry nanoparticle toner
idea: Coat the wafer with a thin amorphous-selenium photoconductor, corona-charge it, expose with patterned light so charge leaks where lit, then cascade charged hardmask nanoparticles that stick only to the charge image; fuse, etch and sublime away the Se.
why: Water and capital: dry, solvent-free patterning on copier-class tooling for coarse periphery/BEOL layers (100s of nm), ~100x cheaper litho for those layers. Resolution is the risk.

title: Ni: nickel-stressor spalling makes kerfless substrates without saw slurry
idea: Sputter a tensile Ni stressor film on an ingot face or reclaimed wafer and peel off a 20-50 um single-crystal Si layer by controlled spalling, then smooth it by H2 anneal and bond it to a carrier, skipping wire sawing, lapping and wet polishing.
why: Water and resources: substrate making drops >10x in water, and kerf-free use roughly halves silicon and quartz-crucible demand per wafer (Spruce Pine >80%).
